readmeExcerpt:
drawDB

Free, simple, and intuitive database schema editor and SQL generator.

DrawDB is a robust and user-friendly database entity relationship diagram (ERD) editor right in your browser. Build diagrams with a few clicks, export and import SQL scripts, generate migrations, customize your editor, and more without creating an account. See the full set of features on [here](https://drawdb.app/). ## Getting Started ### Local Development ```bash git clone https://github.com/drawdb-io/drawdb cd drawdb npm install npm run dev ``` ### Build ```bash git clone https://github.com/drawdb-io/drawdb cd drawdb npm install npm run build ``` ### Docker Build ```bash docker build -t drawdb . docker run -p 3000:80 drawdb ``` If you want to enable sharing, set up the [server](https://github.com/drawdb-io/drawdb-server) and environment variables according to `.env.sample`. This is optional unless you need to share files. With the Docker image, pass the server URL when starting the container. No rebuild is needed: ```bash docker run -p 3000:80 -e VITE_BACKEND_URL=https://your-drawdb-server.example.com ghcr.io/drawdb-io/drawdb:latest ``` ## Contributing Please see [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for guidelines on how to contribute to this project. ## Support - Join discussions: [Discord](https://discord.gg/BrjZgNrmR6)

releases.name: v1.9.0 - Import from your database
releases.body:
## Import from your database

**File → Import from database.** Pick your dialect, copy the read-only query drawDB gives you, run it in the SQL client you already use (psql, Workbench, DBeaver, SSMS…), and paste the result back. drawDB draws the diagram and auto-arranges it.

- Works with PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, SQL Server, SQLite and Oracle
- No connection string: your credentials never leave your machine, and drawDB never sees row data

(#1182)

## Subject areas that hold tables

Areas now own the tables inside them: move an area and its tables move with it, hide or show a whole group at once, and reorder areas. (#1184, #1185)

## Also in this release

- Faster canvas on large diagrams (#1172, #1183)
- SQL headers tab: custom text at the top of every export (#1169)
- Comments shown in the sidebar (#1159)
- Touchpad horizontal panning without holding Shift (#1162)
- Fix: import when `NOT NULL` is absent (#1171)
- Fix: autosave for enum-only diagrams and empty edits (#1186)
- Dependency updates

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/drawdb-io/drawdb/compare/v1.8.2...v1.9.0

readmeHtml:
drawDB

Free, simple, and intuitive database schema editor and SQL generator.

DrawDB is a robust and user-friendly database entity relationship diagram (ERD) editor right in your browser. Build diagrams with a few clicks, export and import SQL scripts, generate migrations, customize your editor, and more without creating an account. See the full set of features on here.

Getting Started

Local Development

git clone https://github.com/drawdb-io/drawdb
cd drawdb
npm install
npm run dev

Build

git clone https://github.com/drawdb-io/drawdb
cd drawdb
npm install
npm run build

Docker Build

docker build -t drawdb .
docker run -p 3000:80 drawdb

If you want to enable sharing, set up the server and environment variables according to .env.sample. This is optional unless you need to share files.

With the Docker image, pass the server URL when starting the container. No rebuild is needed:

docker run -p 3000:80 -e VITE_BACKEND_URL=https://your-drawdb-server.example.com ghcr.io/drawdb-io/drawdb:latest

Contributing

Please see CONTRIBUTING.md for guidelines on how to contribute to this project.

Support

  • Join discussions: Discord

aiSummary.oneLiner: A free, simple, and highly intuitive browser-based database schema editor and SQL generator.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: DrawDB is a robust, open-source entity-relationship diagram editor that runs entirely within the web browser. It allows developers to visually architect complex database schemas, define tables, and configure relationships using a fluid drag-and-drop interface, without requiring a backend server or complex installations. Crucially, the tool can instantly translate visual designs into raw, deployable SQL export scripts tailored for major database systems. This drastically streamlines the initial database architecture phase, enabling rapid prototyping and seamless team collaboration. Everything runs completely client-side in the browser, ensuring data privacy and zero setup overhead.
keyFeatures: Visual Schema Editor: Provide a responsive, drag-and-drop canvas for designing complex relational database architectures.
Multi-Dialect Export: Automatically generate accurate DDL SQL scripts tailored for MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQLite, and SQL Server.
Relationship Mapping: Enable users to easily define and visualize complex foreign key constraints and table relationships.
Browser-Based Execution: Operate entirely client-side, ensuring user privacy and eliminating the need for complex server deployments.
Template Utilization: Offer a variety of pre-built schema templates to kickstart architecture for common application types.

useCases.title: Migration Planning
useCases.description: Teams visually map out complex structural changes when planning significant database migrations or refactors.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Software engineers, database administrators, and technical architects who need a fast, accessible, and visual way to design relational databases and generate deployment scripts. It significantly streamlines the design process for development teams.
